author: Linnaeus, 1758

art.subject: Gyrfalcon (Falco rusticolus), adult grey morph in winter: upperparts slate-grey to grey-brown with pale grey-blue bars and feather edges; head greyish with an indistinct pale supercilium and a thin, weak dark moustachial stripe; underparts white with dark drop-shaped spots on the breast becoming bars on the flanks and thighs; tail grey with fine pale bars. Bill bluish-grey with a dark tip; cere, bare eye-ring, legs and feet yellow; iris dark brown.
art.pose: perched upright on a snow-dusted rock, watching over open ground
art.scene: open coastal fields and dunes of northeastern Korea in midwinter, light snow cover; no people, buildings or text
art.build: Largest falcon, clearly larger and heavier than a Peregrine Falcon, the female approaching a buzzard in size; deep-chested and bulky. Head rounded, neck short. Bill short and strongly hooked, with a notch (tomial tooth) on the upper mandible. Legs short and powerful with feathered thighs. At rest the wingtips fall well short of the tail tip, reaching only about two-thirds down the tail. Wings broad-based, long and pointed but blunter than a Peregrine's; shallow, powerful wingbeats. Tail long and broad, rounded at the tip.
avoid: Do not paint the bold black hood and broad black moustache of Peregrine Falcon (Falco peregrinus); the Gyrfalcon's moustache is thin and faint.
Do not make the wingtips reach the tail tip at rest; they fall well short.
Do not paint a slim, hobby-like build; it is bulky and broad-winged.
Do not mix morphs: this grey bird should not get a white head or white body.
